messages:
customer_success: Heads up — ACME reported persistent 429s to the dedicated endpoint since ~09:30 PST. They say they're on a reserved pool but requests are being throttled. Example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Routing appears to send them to a shared pool. Can someone triage? :rotating_light:

maria-cheung: Thanks — can you paste the request headers and a few request-ids and the tenant header? Suspect something with the tier tag parsing.

customer_success: Pasted headers below (redacted):
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood-inference.internal
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
x-redwood-tenant: acme-corp
x-redwood-tier: platinum;org=acme-corp;region=us-west-2
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
We saw identical requests routed to shared-small pool and throttled at 80 qps while the dedicated gold pool had spare capacity.

devon: Interesting — I saw a staging flake last week where tags with semicolons were not parsed fully. Control plane was using the leftmost token but there was also a truncation when header length > 64. Might be a combined bug: split on ';' but then trim to 3 chars due to an old compatibility branch.

sre_ash: Adding a control-plane eval log snippet I pulled for req_0a1b2c3d: 
```
[controlplane] evaluate_route: tenant=acme-corp, raw_tier=platinum;org=acme-corp;region=us-west-2
[controlplane] normalized_tier=pla
[route_decider] matched_rule: tier=pla -> pool=shared-small
[router] selected_pool=shared-small, reason="rule match"
```
That normalization of 'platinum' -> 'pla' looks wrong and explains the mis-select.

eng-runtime: Confirmed locally — the parser had a legacy path that normalizes tier to first 3 chars when header length > 48 to cope with old clients. That branch should've been removed when we moved to label-based routing. Repro command: 
```bash
curl -H "x-redwood-tier: platinum;org=acme-corp;region=us-west-2" https://controlplane.internal/debug/route?tenant=acme-corp
```
response shows normalized_tier=pla.

maria-cheung: Workaround for now: have ACME set x-rw-target-pool: gold-usw2 in their requests (this bypasses label select). Also setting temporary alert to watch pool headroom directly so autoscaler can spin up capacity even if labels mismatch. Please confirm customer can inject header.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2233. Severity P2. Paging oncall.

devon: Fix plan: remove the legacy 3-char normalization, update token-splitting to split on ';' and '=' properly, add unit + integration tests for long tier headers, and add a controlplane safeguard to prefer explicit x-rw-target-pool header if present. Will open PR and run canary on dedicated pools only.

customer_success: Customer accepted the temporary x-rw-target-pool workaround and provided permission to test with their traffic for the canary. They asked for ETA on the fix.

maria-cheung: ETA: hotfix PR within 12h, CI + internal canary 24–36h after PR merge, full roll 48h after verification. We'll notify Sales/CS to pause escalation steps. :thumbsup:

jamal: Note on customer impact: billing looks normal (no unexpected overage). Throttles hit are the per-pool QPS caps, not tenant quota. Recommend offering a small credit if SLA target missed while we roll the fix.

eng-runtime: Follow-ups: 1) I'll add a regression test for header lengths and semicolon parsing. 2) Add metric for "normalized_tier != raw_tier" to detect future regressions. 3) Ensure autoscaler watches both label selectors and explicit pool annotations.

maria-cheung: Thanks team — assigning owners: devon (parser patch), eng-runtime (tests + metrics), sre_ash (canary + rollout), customer_success (communicate ETA). Will update thread when PR is open.
